We know that $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\sin x)=\cos x,$ and that $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\cos x)=-\sin x.$ Applying these formulas and the sum and constant multiple rules, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} &= \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(- 16 \cos{\left(x \right)} + \frac{8}{x^{2}}) \\ &= (16 \sin{\left(x \right)})+(- \frac{16}{x^{3}}) \\ &= 16 \sin{\left(x \right)} - \frac{16}{x^{3}}.\end{aligned}

question.:question/problem: What is the slope of the tangent line to the curve $y=16 x - 40 \cos{\left(x \right)}$ at the point $x=\frac{\pi}{6}$?
question.:question/worked-solution:
The slope is the derivative evaluated at $x=\frac{\pi}{6}.$

We know that $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\sin x)=\cos x,$ and that $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\cos x)=-\sin x.$ Applying these formulas and the sum and constant multiple rules, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} &= \frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(16 x - 40 \cos{\left(x \right)}) \\ &= (40 \sin{\left(x \right)})+(16) \\ &= 40 \sin{\left(x \right)} + 16.\end{aligned}
$$

Evaluating at $x=\frac{\pi}{6},$ we get

$$
y^{\prime}(\frac{\pi}{6})=16+40\sin(\frac{\pi}{6})=16+40\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)=36.
$$

Therefore, the slope is $36.$
